HasUponPickupEffect.rationale: Pear.cs:13 `HasUponPickupEffect => true`; the flag feeds RelicModel.IsTradable, mirrored at relics/base.py:126-136, so an Uncommon relic that has already paid out is correctly excluded from the trade events on both sides. Matches.

AfterObtained.rationale: Pear.cs:17-20 is `await CreatureCmd.GainMaxHp(base.Owner.Creature, base.DynamicVars.MaxHp.BaseValue)`. CanonicalVars is `new MaxHpVar(10m)` (line 15) with no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so MAX_HP = 10 (pear.py:16) is the pinned non-ascension value. GainMaxHp is SetMaxHp followed by `Heal(num)` for the same amount (CreatureCmd.cs:786-799), and run.gain_max_hp is `self.max_hp += amount; self.heal(amount)` (run.py:311-314) -- so the +10 max HP AND the accompanying +10 heal both land, which is the half a port easily drops. The MapPointHistoryEntry bookkeeping at CreatureCmd.cs:793-797 is a run-history statistic with no sim counterpart and no effect on play. IMPORTANT CONTRAST checked deliberately: audit/records/relic/big_mushroom.json records a LIVE gap for a max-HP relic whose port implements NO after_obtained at all, so the +20 lived only in the event that granted it; Pear does implement it, and `run.add_relic` really does invoke it (run.py:550-552), so the same defect is not present here.

undo_after_obtained (no C# counterpart).issue: RE-VERDICTED from deliberate-divergence to gap by the 2026-07-26 relic fix pass, so that all five implementers of this mechanism agree (binding rule 3). PROMPT.md v6 item 3 already states the rule: the ABSENCE of `undo_after_obtained` is faithful everywhere, but an undo that EXISTS and CLAMPS instead of subtracting violates its own stated contract, and 'all five implementers do it'. Four of the five are already gaps -- relic/mango G1, relic/strawberry G, relic/lees_waffle N4, relic/looming_fruit N3 -- and pear was the lone dissenter. THE OLD RATIONALE IS TRUE AND IRRELEVANT: 'granting then un-granting on a FULL-HP player returns exactly the starting state' holds only for a player at full HP, and the relic is granted on a DAMAGED player in the general case. sts2_rl/relics/pear.py:21-25 is the same shape as sts2_rl/relics/mango.py:21-25 -- `run.lose_max_hp(MAX_HP)` then `run.hp = min(run.hp, run.max_hp)` -- and `RunState.lose_max_hp` (sts2_rl/run.py:315-321) only CLAMPS current HP to the new maximum; it never gives back the heal `gain_max_hp` (sts2_rl/run.py:310-313) paid out. EXECUTED at 75/80 for all five implementers: lees_waffle (75,80) -> (87,87) -> (80,80); looming_fruit (75,80) -> (106,111) -> (80,80); mango (75,80) -> (89,94) -> (80,80); pear (75,80) -> (85,90) -> (80,80); strawberry (75,80) -> (82,87) -> (80,80). Every one ends at (80,80) instead of (75,80) -- a silent +5 current HP. OBSERVABLE and LIVE where the helper runs: `undo_after_obtained` has exactly one caller, the conformance runner's relic resync (sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:455-461), so this cannot be reached from play -- but that caller exists precisely to keep DETECTOR 3's act-boundary HP assertion honest, and the leak makes the sim read HIGH for the rest of the run, which is the assertion's whole subject. It is a gap in the tool the audit's liveness rests on, not a fidelity gap against the C# (there is no C# counterpart to diverge from) -- graded C, conformance-only. FIX: subtract the heal explicitly (`run.hp = min(run.hp, run.max_hp); run.hp -= MAX_HP` clamped at 1, or snapshot hp/max_hp at grant time), at all five sites at once. Rule 7: sts2_rl/run.py, sts2_rl/relics/mango.py and sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py are cited and not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: GainMaxHp's argument validation and the accompanying heal (CreatureCmd.cs:786-799)
guards.rationale: C# throws on a negative amount and heals by the amount SetMaxHp actually returned (which can differ from the requested amount if a max-HP cap applied); the sim heals by the literal 10 after raising max HP by 10, and no ported effect caps max HP, so the two are equal. Checked because the heal is the part that is easy to lose and the part a player notices.

guards.what: N2 (PROMPT.md bug class 16): no RelicModel.IsAllowed override; no Rng draw; no state
guards.rationale: Executed grep over the batch's fifteen C# relic files finds no IsAllowed override, so sweep B's 17-relic pool-eligibility cluster excludes this unit -- worth confirming rather than assuming, because several other one-shot pickup relics (dragon_fruit, girya, meal_ticket) ARE in that cluster and Pear looks just like them. The relic draws no Rng and holds no fields, so bug classes 13 and 16 have nothing to bite on, consistent with its absence from sweep-reset's candidate list. Obtainability confirmed by execution (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b11.py pool`): Uncommon in the transcribed grab bag.

guards.what: N3: the port implements no combat hooks at all, and none are dropped
guards.rationale: Pear.cs has exactly three members -- Rarity, HasUponPickupEffect, CanonicalVars -- plus AfterObtained, so there is no behavioural override for the port to miss. This is one of the very few genuinely complete behaviourless-beyond-pickup ports; sweep C (.superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md) counts 2 such stubs among 37, and unlike the other 35 there is no false premise here because the port DOES implement the one hook that matters.
